- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

Everything you pasted is live, and Cyrus is still a **no-go** for private beta on one remaining blocker.

|---|---|
| Alerts timer | Fixed |

| Nightly backup | **Still failing.** It needs your backup public key and an off-box target |

Cyrus on Minecraft works end to end. What is left splits into things only you can do, things I can do now, and things to do after launch.

**Eval so far:** 7 of 7 builds on 0.16 have succeeded and the 8th is running. That is early, and the full number comes at 90 builds.

## 1. Only you can unblock (these gate going public)
| Item | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Anthropic API key** | The build service runs on your personal subscription login, which isn't allowed for a public service. It also shares session limits with me, which caused the "session limit" failures. |
| **Backup public key and off-box target** | Nightly backup is the last private-beta blocker, and `/tank` is a single disk. |
| **Real-client test (10 minutes)** | Run a build and join the server with real Minecraft. Nothing I run can prove it feels right in game. |
| **Prices, plan sizes and slot counts** | 44 settings are still placeholders. |
| **Terms, privacy and sound-library licence review** | This needs a lawyer or you. |
| **Discord alert webhook and beta tester emails** | Alerts are journal-only and no one is allow-listed. |
| **Stripe live-mode test purchase** | The key is live but no real purchase has been run through the token flow. |

## 2. I can do now, no input needed
- **Final eval number on 0.16.** It's running, and the gate is accepted as the baseline once it finishes.
- **Footer legal links** on the landing page (a launch-check warning).
- **Tighten the nginx fallback** to an explicit list of public files and add the missing routes to the regex.
- **Free 1.5 GB** to get `/` under 80% (clearing staging build output, with your yes).
- **26.x lane.** Minecraft 26.x preview support is not built yet.
- **Weak spots the eval shows.** I will fix whichever prompt types fail first-try once the numbers land.
- **Re-run launch-check** until beta says GO.

## 3. Quality "perfection" work (post-beta, ranked)
1. **Self-learning loop:** feed real failed builds back into the failure rules automatically (the engine exists, the real data doesn't yet).
2. **Modrinth knowledge distillation:** stages S0–S3 are built, and further coverage will improve complex mods.
3. **Heavier mod types:** custom models and creatures, worldgen and armor lanes have tests but little real-world exposure.
4. **Featured mods and the master mod "The Gloam":** content work, not engineering.
5. **Second game:** Rust and Palworld branches are parked until Minecraft is stable.

**Fastest route to a beta:** you send the backup key and tester emails, I flip the check to GO, then you do the 10-minute real-client test. Public launch then waits on the API key, prices and legal.

content.text:
The Dropbox backups are fixed and verified on real Dropbox.

## What was wrong
The Dropbox login was fine (2.64 TiB free). The old offsite timer had been disabled since 2026-09-15, and the Cyrus backups had been built but never installed. The SFX library and the build VM had no copy anywhere.

## What now runs
| Category | When | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Databases | daily 03:50 | nxeon, nxeon_staging, Cyrus tables |
| Nodes | daily 05:40 | host config for primary and node-2 |
| Apps | daily 06:10 | source bundle and encrypted env |
| VM archives | Sundays 06:30 | newest 2 per VM (about 130 GB) |
| Cyrus library, packs and VM data | daily 03:40 | restic repo on Dropbox |
| Restore drill | Mondays 07:30 | restores the newest dump into a throwaway DB |

Everything is encrypted with `age` and verified after upload. Each run writes a manifest with sizes and checksums. Retention is 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly.

The first real uploads passed `rclone check`. The restore drill restored `nxeon_staging` (230 tables, 144 users) into a throwaway database and dropped it. Production was only read. The launch check's `backup-fresh` row now passes.

## Needs you
1. **Move the two private keys off the server.** They are `/root/OWNER-RETRIEVE-backup-age.key` and `/root/OWNER-RETRIEVE-cyrus-backup-gpg-private.asc`. Without them the backups can't be restored, and with them on the box they protect nothing. Then shred the on-box copies.
2. **Rotate the Dropbox token.** The agent printed it during its work, and session transcripts sync to GitHub. Treat it as exposed.
3. **Discord webhook:** failures only reach in-app notifications until it's set.

## Gaps
- **Not backed up:** node-3/4/5 (stale since 09-16) and node-7 (no SSH route found). I need SSH details or the script installed there.
- **First big runs not done yet:** the 51 GB SFX upload tonight at 03:40 and the 130 GB VM archives on Sunday. Primary RAM and swap are tight, so I'll watch the first Sunday run.
- **Cleanup candidate:** `/tank/backup/platform` holds 465 GB, including archives of deleted VMs. I left it alone.

The full report is in `agent-notes/BACKUP-REPORT-2026-10-14.md`, and the exact owner steps are in `agent-notes/BACKUP-DROPBOX-OWNER-STEPS.md`. Four agents are still running: emails, cyrus.my landing, file manager and Cyrus quality.

content.text:
The email overhaul is built and verified, and it is ready to promote.

## What it does
- **One shared dark "Nexion" email layout** now carries every automated email: logo header, navy card with a violet-to-cyan edge, icon tiles, gradient buttons and a footer. It is table-based, works at 600px and matches your mockup.
- **Rebuilt templates:** flash sale, TRIAL798 promo, GPU restock, VM-move notice, growth scoreboard, a new budget alert, and the Cyrus notification mail.
- **Plain-text versions** are now built properly, with no CSS leaking in.
- The gameplay section is reverted and none of it is committed, as you asked.

## Tracking is intact
- The open pixel, click rewrite, secret-link exemption and one-click unsubscribe headers are untouched.
- A test compares every template's links against a baseline captured from main, so a lost hook fails the build.
- All 58 templates render. `tsc` is clean and the overhaul tests (63) plus related email tests pass.

## Worth knowing
- **Dark emails vs Gmail primary tab:** an old code comment says light emails reach the primary tab more reliably. The agent followed your dark mockup anyway. Watch for promo-tab placement after the first sends.
- **Left alone on purpose:** cold and outreach mail (plain, with its own compliance footer) and the admin digest.
- **Logo path:** the `/brand/logo-email.png` logo can only be confirmed after deploy.
- **Social icons:** there is no social icon row, because I won't invent links.

The branch is `feature/nx-marketing-emails`, commit `f51c539a`, not merged or deployed. I'll bundle it with the other branches into one promote when the rest land, so you only paste once.

Still running: the cyrus.my landing (off demo mode plus the gameplay gallery), the admin file manager, and the Cyrus quality bundle.

  - **Hero animation:** it is labelled as an illustration and types into the placeholder only. The fake build on submit, the fake "Advanced" panel, the fake API-key "Connect" form and the invented `survival-01` server are gone.

  - **Gameplay gallery:** nothing was built. Copy the 7 PNGs and the card text somewhere readable (for example `/root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/gameplay-shots/`) and re-run the task. `publish.sh` caps size at 40 MB, so 7 images at 1600px webp fit.
